statement.p: Find the slope of the tangent line to the curve defined by 2x^{4}-4xy+5y^{2} = 386 at the point ( -3,-8 ).
The slope of the curve at the point (-3, -8) is .

solution.p: Differentiating implicitly with respect to x gives 8x^{3}-4y-4x\, \frac{dy}{dx}+10y\, \frac{dy}{dx} = 0, or \left(10y-4x\right)\, \frac{dy}{dx} = -(8x^{3}-4y), and so \frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{8x^{3}-4y}{10y-4x}. Hence, the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the given point is \frac{dy}{dx} \bigg \vert _ {(x, y) = (-3, -8)} = -\frac{8\mathopen{}\left(-3\right)^{3}-4\cdot \left(-8\right)}{10\cdot \left(-8\right)-4\cdot \left(-3\right)} \textstyle =-\frac{184}{68} =-{\frac{46}{17}}.
